CONFIDENTIALGROWTH PLAYBOOK

Social Media Ad Playbook

How we use paid + organic ads on Instagram and Facebook to recruit a salesforce, drive them to a landing page, and let them try the product before they sign up. Includes an interactive income calculator and 10 ready-to-post ad creatives (5 English, 5 Spanish).

1. The whole idea in one line

We run bold, aspirational ads that promise a real income opportunity - $50K to $100K a year with zero investment - send clickers to a landing page where they can tap a live demo card themselves, and convert them into signed-up reps who order cards and start selling. The ad's only job is to get the click. The landing page's only job is to make them believe it works and sign up.

2. What you're actually selling

The product is a simple, premium review device a business keeps on the counter or window. A customer taps it (NFC) or scans the QR, and it opens the review flow. It comes as an acrylic table stand, a window sticker, or a wallet-size card - same technology. Here is the on-brand look, in English and Spanish:

Design is fully customizable per business and per platform (Google, Yelp, Facebook). We show "We'd love your feedback" because our flow sends everyone through a quick feedback step first (compliant), then on to the public review - it is not a review-gating "Google only" card.

3. Who we target

  • Side-hustlers & gig workers - rideshare, delivery, servers who want daytime income.
  • Students & young adults - comfortable on their phone, want flexible cash.
  • Direct-sales / MLM veterans - already know how to pitch, hate inventory. This has none.
  • Bilingual communities - the Spanish creatives open a huge, under-served recruiting pool.

Paid targeting (Meta Ads): ages 18-45, interests in "side hustle / extra income / entrepreneurship / direct sales," plus a broad Advantage+ audience. Retarget anyone who visited the landing page but did not sign up.

Stacked across a full-time effort, that builds into a six-figure yearly income - which the calculator below lets a recruit prove to themselves.

6. Why the $50K-$100K claim is real (and defensible)

The big number is not made up - it is the math of the offer at a full-time pace, counting the full residual on every subscriber. Each business on the $15/month plan pays you $5/month for 12 months - $60 total - and that is true no matter which month you sign them. So a full year of selling locks in a full 12 months of residual on everyone, even people you sign in month 11 or 12 (some of that money simply lands in year 2, but it is already yours). Same assumptions as the calculator:

EffortCards/dayCard income/yrResidual ($60 each)Total earned
Part-time2$11,520~$8,600~$20,000
Full-time5$28,800~$21,600~$50,000
Top performer10$57,600~$43,200~$100,000

These use a conservative ~25% attach rate (share of businesses that take the monthly plan), which lands the full-time case right at $50K and the top performer at $100K - exactly matching the ads. We say "up to" and "top reps" because 5-10 sales/day is a genuine full-time pace, not what a casual seller hits. Assumes subscribers stay ~12 months; earnings vary and are not guaranteed.

7. Organic vs. paid - run both

ChannelHow to use itCost
Organic postsPost 3-5x/week rotating these creatives. Pin the best one. Reply to every comment fast.Free
Stories / ReelsRe-cut the 4:5 images as full-screen stories with "link in bio." Add a 10-sec clip of a rep counting cash.Free
Paid ads (Meta)Boost the 2-3 best performers. Objective: Leads or Traffic to the landing page. Start $10-20/day per market.$300-600/mo
Local groupsPost the income creatives in city buy/sell/jobs Facebook groups where rules allow.Free

8. A/B test to find the winner

  1. Run 3-4 creatives at once, same budget/audience, for 4-5 days.
  2. Kill the bottom half by cost-per-click and cost-per-signup. Do not judge by likes.
  3. Pour budget into the winner, then make 2 variations of it and repeat.
  4. Test hook angles: "big income" (ad 1) vs "zero cost" (ad 2) vs "no experience" (ad 3) vs "quit your job" (ad 4) vs "easiest sale" (ad 5).

Important: keep the income claims defensible

Meta and the FTC scrutinize big income promises. Every creative already carries an "earnings vary / not guaranteed" line - keep it there. Always phrase potential as "you can earn" / "up to" / "top reps," never "you will make" or "guaranteed." Back the numbers with the calculator and the table in section 6. This keeps the ads bold but inside Facebook/Instagram ad policy so the account does not get banned.
